questions.prompt: Which statement is a falsifiable scientific hypothesis?
options: On 200 held-out scenes, the planner's success rate exceeds the baseline's by at least 5 points under a 1 s limit
The method works well in most cases, so it is better than the existing ones
The robot is intelligent if it never fails at any task it is given
Our algorithm is more elegant than the baseline and therefore a clear improvement
questions.explanation: It names a metric, a comparison, a population and a threshold, so a measurement can contradict it. The others cannot be refuted by any observation.

questions.prompt: A full-factorial ablation has 4 binary design choices and each condition is run with 3 seeds. How many training runs are needed? Give an integer.
Four repeated measurements have sample standard deviation 3.0 (computed with n-1). What is the standard error of the mean? Give 2 decimals.
Controller A scores 8, 6, 9 and controller B scores 5, 6, 4 on the same three seeds. What is the mean of the paired differences A-B? Give 2 decimals.
A new vision pipeline is compared with the old one, but it was also trained on twice as much data. What can be concluded?
options: The new pipeline is better; more data is irrelevant
The difference cannot be attributed to the pipeline alone
The result is invalid because bigger datasets are always unfair
The new pipeline is better only if the gain is above 10%
questions.explanation: The change in data size is confounded with the change in method: a gain cannot be attributed to the new pipeline without a control (same data) or an ablation.

questions.prompt: You test 10 independent variants, none of which truly has any effect, each at level 0.05. What is the probability that at least one appears significant? Give 3 decimals.
Which reporting practice gives the most honest picture of a stochastic training method?
options: All seeds, with mean and an interval, plus the raw values
The seed that the baseline performed worst on
One seed, fixed in advance, so the result is reproducible
Only the best seed, to show what the method can do
questions.explanation: Reporting all seeds with a mean and interval avoids selection bias; best-seed or tuned-seed reporting overstates performance.

questions.prompt: An integrator's error drops from 4.0e-2 to 4.0e-4 when the step size is reduced by a factor of 10. What is the observed order of convergence? Give an integer.
A 95% confidence interval for the mean improvement of A over B is [-0.5, 3.3] points. Which conclusion is justified?
options: A is better than B with 95% probability, since most of the interval is positive
A is worse than B, because the lower end of the interval is negative
The data do not rule out zero improvement; more data are needed to decide
There is a 5% chance that A is better, as the interval covers zero
questions.explanation: The interval includes 0, so the data are compatible with no improvement; it does not show that there is none, and it is not a probability statement about this fixed interval.

questions.prompt: A vision model improved after you added augmentation and more data at the same time. Design the experiment that separates the two effects and state what conclusions remain limited.
rubric: Uses a 2x2 design: (augmentation off/on) x (small/large data), with matched seeds, training budget and evaluation set
Reads the main effects and the interaction, and reports intervals over several seeds
States limits: one dataset/task/architecture, no hardware transfer, hyperparameters tuned for only some conditions
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write the key fields of a one-page protocol for comparing two controllers in simulation, and say which of them must be fixed before looking at any results.
rubric: Includes hypothesis, metric, scenes/initial conditions, seeds, budgets and controls, environment/versions, success criterion
States that the metric, success criterion, seeds and exclusion rules are fixed in advance
Says deviations are reported and exploratory findings are separated from confirmatory ones
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Explain why choosing the best of 50 model variants by its test-set score gives an optimistic estimate, and how to repair the protocol.
rubric: Explains the winner's-curse selection effect: the maximum of noisy scores is biased upward
Proposes a separate validation split (or cross-validation) for selection and a single final evaluation on untouched test data
Mentions reporting how many variants were tried
